svg.aria-label: How each decision calls the models, with one recorded decision from the release 53 smoke as the example. Belief: one forward of the unified transformer on the public history returns each card's odds of being in each hand, drawn as a heatmap; 64 deals are sampled from it, drawn as tiles, and all 64 are consistent with earlier play. Prior: no new forward; the same trunk's policy head scores every card; the 24 legal plays are drawn as bars and the top 8 are admitted, the ace of hearts and the pair of aces of hearts first at log-odds −0.43. Value: the unified model's readout scores each of the 8 plays in all 64 deals, 512 rows, 192 of them from the decision's memo, drawn as an 8 by 64 heatmap with a row-mean column; the best average was the three of diamonds at 1.350. Endgame: with 7 cards or fewer, no model call; each deal is solved exactly by a game tree with all hands face up and pruned branches, and the per-deal results are averaged; it switched to the pair of aces of hearts, 1.469 against 1.422 for the three of diamonds. It played the pair of aces of hearts in 0.17 seconds. One unified transformer gives the belief, the prior, the leaf values and the reply ranking; all models run in NumPy on the server CPU with a 3 second budget per play; the trump call and the bury use the G3 value model.
svg.title: One decision, four steps
svg.text: Example: one lead with 7 cards left, from the release 53 smoke. Numbers are real; cell shades, tiles and tree shape are illustrative.
One unified transformer gives belief, prior, values and replies · NumPy on the server CPU · 3 s per play · trump call and bury use the G3 value model
